item.title: California passes bills to force data‑center energy and water disclosures
item.description:
California passes bills to force data‑center energy and water disclosures

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed seven bills on Monday that aim to increase transparency around data centers’ electricity and water consumption.

🔍 Overview

  • Data centers are expanding across the U.S., prompting protests over potential strain on power grids and local water supplies.
  • The new California legislation seeks to give communities better data and more say on how data centers impact electricity bills and water supply.

🧩 Legislative Details

Bill Requirement
SB 886, SB 1168, AB 2383 Direct the California Public Utilities Commission to create separate power rates for data centers to recoup grid‑connection costs
AB 1577 Requires monthly reporting on data centers’ energy consumption
AB 2619, AB 2469 Require water‑use disclosures; AB 2469 also makes operators cover infrastructure‑upgrade costs
SB 887 Removes categorical exemptions from the California Environmental Quality Act, ensuring data centers undergo environmental review

⚙️ Why it matters

  • Without clear data, scientists have found it “extremely frustrating to try to understand basic information,” says Mark Specht, senior manager for the climate and energy program at the Union of Concerned Scientists.
  • The disclosure rules begin next year but still won’t provide a full picture of consumption.
  • Two possible outcomes are outlined: (1) ballooning electricity demand could lead to costly new infrastructure that may be overbuilt if AI demand falls, passing costs to other consumers; (2) spreading fixed grid‑maintenance costs across more customers could lower electricity rates, but this depends on data centers contributing to distribution‑system costs rather than only connecting to high‑voltage transmission.
  • Water‑use data remain opaque; water providers have refused to share usage figures, and current disclosures only apply when seeking permits or business licenses, leaving year‑to‑year usage unclear.

📊 Perspectives

  • “I’m happy [AB 1577] passed,” Specht said, noting the difficulty in researching state offers.
  • “I wouldn’t say definitively that data centers have increased the cost [of electricity],” he added, acknowledging the lack of numbers to demonstrate either increase or potential savings.
  • As data centers’ power needs grow, monitoring their energy and water consumption becomes increasingly important.

#California #DataCenters #EnergyPolicy #WaterUse

Source: Data centers are black boxes, but California wants to change that

item.title: NVIDIA Open Sources NodeWright for Kubernetes Host Infrastructure Management
item.description:
NVIDIA Open Sources NodeWright for Kubernetes Host Infrastructure Management

NVIDIA has released NodeWright as an open-source, Kubernetes-native package manager designed to modify and maintain host infrastructure at scale. As part of the NVIDIA DSX OS open-source software layer, NodeWright enables the declarative configuration and safe updating of Kubernetes node operating systems without disrupting workloads.

🔍 Overview

NodeWright is a component of the NVIDIA DSX platform, which treats entire facilities as single systems (AI factories) rather than collections of machines. It is part of the supporting infrastructure capabilities that include:

  • NVIDIA GPU Operator
  • NVIDIA Network Operator
  • Topograph
  • DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs
  • NVIDIA Cluster Readiness Engine (NVCRE)
  • NVSentinel

🧩 How it works

NodeWright consists of three main components:

Component Description
Operator A Kubernetes controller that watches for custom resources and manages the lifecycle of changes across nodes.
Custom Resources Used to define NodeWright packages; these deploy via tools such as kubectl, Helm, Argo CD, or Flux.
Packages Container images containing binaries, configurations, scripts, and verification scripts to surface failures and stop incorrect rollouts.

When applying changes, NodeWright follows a specific operational flow:

  1. Cordon: Marks the node as unschedulable.
  2. Wait: Allows critical workloads to finish gracefully.
  3. Drain: Evicts remaining pods, honoring PodDisruptionBudgets by default.
  4. Apply and configure: Runs the package to set kernel parameters, install agents, and configure system services.
  5. Interrupt: Restarts a service or reboots the node if required.
  6. Uncordon: Returns the node to the cluster for workloads.

⚙️ Key details

NodeWright manages the full lifecycle of host-level changes, including installation, configuration, upgrade, and uninstallation. Key capabilities include:

  • Infrastructure Operations: Performs tasks that normally require root access without recycling nodes, such as setting sysctl and GRUB parameters, configuring crash dump collection, creating logical volumes, installing security agents, and remediating CVEs.
  • Workload Awareness: Respects Kubernetes primitives including node selectors, taints, tolerations, and PodDisruptionBudgets.
  • State Tracking: Tracks the semantic version and state of every package on every node to distinguish between fresh installations, upgrades, and downgrades.
  • Dependency Management: Uses declared dependencies to determine the correct execution order.

🚀 Availability

NodeWright is available as open source and has run in production at NVIDIA under the name Skyhook.

#NVIDIA #Kubernetes #OpenSource #Infrastructure #CloudNative

Source: Manage Kubernetes Node Fleets with NodeWright | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: NVIDIA Releases Open Source Cluster Readiness Engine for Kubernetes
item.description:
NVIDIA Releases Open Source Cluster Readiness Engine for Kubernetes

NVIDIA has introduced the Cluster Readiness Engine (NVCRE), an open source Kubernetes controller designed to identify hardware and configuration issues in GPU clusters before production workloads are deployed.

💡 Why it matters

Standard diagnostics can report that every GPU, network link, and pod is healthy, yet a 512-GPU training job may still underperform or fail. Potential causes include:

  • A single slow GPU.
  • A link that degrades under load.
  • A configuration that routes traffic over a slower path.

Without specialized tooling, operators may only discover these problems hours into a run or via customer tickets, leading to days of manual cluster bisection while capacity remains idle. NVCRE transforms readiness from an assumption into a proven property by running real distributed workloads that expose hardware problems.

⚙️ Key details

On Slurm, testing readiness requires a single srun command, but Kubernetes lacks a built-in equivalent. Running such tests on Kubernetes typically requires manual GPU and RDMA resource requests, NCCL settings matched to the network fabric, large shared-memory volumes, and mechanisms to ensure pods start together. NVCRE fills these gaps, removing the need for operators to:

  • Write NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) manifests by hand.
  • Bisect racks manually.
  • Rely on customer tickets to learn about degraded hardware.

NVCRE supports a staged readiness process where clusters move through bring-up, burn-in, preproduction, and production, with each stage setting a different bar. This replaces the need for platform teams to maintain custom runbooks, spreadsheets, or shell scripts wrapped around NCCL tests.

🧩 How it works

NVCRE uses an API based on Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs), allowing management through GitOps workflows and inspection via kubectl. The system uses a three-resource hierarchy to attribute failures to specific nodes and categories:

Resource Function
Certification The top-level resource that names the nodes to test and the categories to run.
Workflow Manages one category; applies overrides, manages iteration count, sets the orchestration target, and creates the child job.
Job Runs the workload for the target node group, monitors health, and records measurements and failures.

Results propagate upward from the Job to the Workflow and finally to the Certification. This allows the system to name exactly which node caused a failure, such as reporting that one GPU hit a hardware fault during NCCL while another missed its bandwidth target.

#NVIDIA #Kubernetes #GPU #OpenSource #ClusterManagement

Source: Validate GPU Cluster Readiness Before AI Workloads Land | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: AI Advancements Heighten Cyber Risks to Aging Critical Infrastructure
item.description:
AI Advancements Heighten Cyber Risks to Aging Critical Infrastructure

The rapid development of AI capabilities is enabling adversaries to execute cyberattacks against critical infrastructure more efficiently, compounding the vulnerabilities of aging equipment designed long before modern cybersecurity threats emerged.

🔍 Overview

Critical infrastructure in the United States, such as the power sector, frequently relies on hardware with a lifespan of several decades, with the average nuclear reactor now approximately 44 years old. These legacy systems, often controlled by operational technology (OT) that does not support frequent software patching, are increasingly susceptible to attacks.

⚙️ Key details

AI is lowering the barrier to entry for adversaries by providing technical knowledge that may have been previously unavailable to them:

  • AI models can analyze manuals and internal systems to help less-skilled actors understand OT protocols and networks.
  • Adversaries use AI to chain vulnerabilities together and automate processes from initial access to exploitation.
  • Research associates, such as Sophie McDowall of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, note that AI allows adversaries to move faster than defenders can respond.

💡 Why it matters

As threats evolve, experts are emphasizing the need for defensive strategies beyond traditional IT security. Strategies include:

  • Ensuring infrastructure can switch to manual operations when necessary.
  • Reducing the interconnectedness of systems to limit exposure.
  • Moving toward a policy of disconnecting systems that cannot be effectively protected.
Expert Role/Organization
Sophie McDowall Research Associate, Foundation for Defense of Democracies
Rob Denaburg Cybersecurity Program Senior Manager, American Public Power Association
Joshua Corman Executive in Residence, Institute for Security and Technology

#Cybersecurity #CriticalInfrastructure #AI #OTSecurity

Source: Humans, not rogue AI, are still the biggest cybersecurity risk to energy systems

item.title: Integrating NVIDIA Resiliency Extension with PyTorch FSDP on Amazon EKS
item.description:
Integrating NVIDIA Resiliency Extension with PyTorch FSDP on Amazon EKS

NVIDIA Resiliency Extension (NVRx) has been integrated into PyTorch Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) training on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to address training interruptions and I/O bottlenecks in large-scale distributed jobs.

💡 Why it matters

Large-scale distributed training jobs running across dozens of nodes for hours or days face statistically inevitable interruptions such as network partitions, memory errors, software exceptions, or infrastructure events. A single GPU fault can trigger a cascade where NVIDIA Collective Communication Library (NCCL) timeouts propagate to healthy workers and pods crash, resulting in expensive GPU hours with zero training progress. Additionally, synchronous checkpointing can consume up to 40% of total wall time by blocking all ranks on I/O.

🧩 How it works

NVRx is a pip-installable Python layer (pip install nvidia-resiliency-ext) that adds fault-tolerance primitives to PyTorch without requiring custom kernels, a PyTorch fork, or recompilation. These primitives drop into existing FSDP scripts as ordinary imports, leaving the model and training code untouched.

Feature Function Fault Class Handled
Async Checkpointing Uses TorchAsyncCheckpoint to replace torch.save with async_save(), handing state dicts to a background process to overlap I/O with training. I/O Bottlenecks
In-process Restart Uses inprocess.Wrapper to wrap the train function; it aborts the active process group, runs health checks, and re-rendezvouses survivors. Soft faults (unhandled exceptions, NCCL hangs)
ft_launcher An in-job restart launcher that uses RankMonitorClient to check heartbeats and respawn fresh workers on stall or death. Hard faults (SIGKILL, OOM kill, OS-level hangs)

⚙️ Key details

  • Async Checkpointing: Paired with FSDP LOCAL_STATE_DICT, each rank writes its own shard directly to avoid all-gather and rank-0 bottlenecks. A finalize_async_save() call commits the write before the next save.
  • In-process Recovery: The CUDA allocator, interpreter, and outer-scope objects survive the restart.
  • In-job Recovery: The launcher kills survivors, reclaims GPU memory, and respawns workers who reload from the latest checkpoint.
  • Infrastructure: The solution runs on Amazon EKS using self-managed node groups of p5.48xlarge instances, featuring 8 NVIDIA H100 80 GB GPUs and 32 Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) network interfaces per instance.
  • Validation: Benchmark results were collected on H100 GPUs at a scale of 2 to 8 nodes.

#PyTorch #NVIDIA #AmazonEKS #FSDP #GPU

Source: Fault tolerant distributed training on Amazon EKS using NVRx | Amazon Web Services

item.title: New Deployment Specifications for Kubernetes Cluster Infrastructure
item.description:
New Deployment Specifications for Kubernetes Cluster Infrastructure

A new infrastructure deployment specification has been released, supporting highly available clusters across a wide range of cloud providers and Linux distributions.

🚀 Availability

The system can be deployed on the following platforms:

  • AWS
  • GCE
  • Azure
  • OpenStack
  • vSphere
  • Equinix Metal (bare metal)
  • Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (Experimental)
  • Baremetal

⚙️ Key details

Supported Operating Systems

The system supports most popular Linux distributions, including:

  • Debian Bookworm, Trixie
  • Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, 26.04
  • CentOS Stream / RHEL 9, 10
  • Fedora 39, 40, 41, 42
  • Fedora CoreOS
  • openSUSE Leap 16.x/Tumbleweed
  • Oracle Linux 9, 10
  • Alma Linux 9, 10
  • Rocky Linux 9, 10 (experimental in 10)
  • Flatcar Container Linux by Kinvolk
  • Kylin Linux Advanced Server V10 (experimental)
  • Amazon Linux 2 (experimental)
  • UOS Linux (experimental)
  • openEuler (experimental)

Note: Upstart/SysV init based OS types are not supported.

Component Versions

Component Version
kubernetes 1.36.4
etcd 3.6.14
docker 28.3
containerd 2.3.5
cri-o 1.36.5 (experimental; Fedora, Ubuntu, and CentOS based OS only)
cni-plugins 1.9.1
calico 3.31.7
cilium 1.20.2
flannel 0.28.9
kube-ovn 1.12.21
kube-router 2.1.1
multus 4.2.2
kube-vip 1.0.3

🧩 How it works

  • Composable: Users have a choice of the network plugin for instances.
  • Testing: The system utilizes continuous integration tests.

item.title: Survey Finds Majority of Likely Voters Oppose AI Data Center Construction
item.description:
Survey Finds Majority of Likely Voters Oppose AI Data Center Construction

A survey of 1,503 likely voters conducted in early September reveals that 61 percent of respondents oppose the construction of data centers used to power AI technology, while 14 percent say they strongly support it.

⚙️ Key details

Opposition to AI data centers varies by political affiliation and voter demographic:

  • Donald Trump voters: Split nearly evenly with 49 percent support and 45 percent oppose.
  • Kamala Harris voters: 74 percent lean oppose.
  • Non-voters: 67 percent lean oppose.
  • Age demographics: AI and data centers registered at less than 1 percent for most demographics, except for the 18–29 group, where 3 percent selected this issue over other popular responses such as inflation, foreign policy, and the economy.

Among those who oppose the construction of data centers, 56 percent support limits, while 38 percent prefer a total ban.

💡 Why it matters

Respondents cited several specific reasons for their opposition:

Reason for Opposition Percentage
Environment/water usage 32%
Impact on local communities 21%
General distrust or dislike of AI 18%
Regulation concerns 10%
The economy 9%

Regarding trust in handling the issue, 40 percent of 554 respondents favored Democrats and 42 percent favored Republicans, while 18 percent refused or did not know. This follows previous polling, including a March NBC News poll where AI polled lower than ICE, and a May Gallup poll showing seven in ten Americans opposed local construction of AI data centers.

#AI #DataCenters #PublicOpinion #Infrastructure

Source: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll

item.title: Hyperscalers Invest Trillions in AI Data Center Infrastructure
item.description:
Hyperscalers Invest Trillions in AI Data Center Infrastructure

A group of AI hyperscalers is investing massive amounts of capital to build AI data centers, representing one of the largest capital investments by any industry in history.

⚙️ Key details

  • Investments:
    • Hyperscalers will spend about $750 billion this year.
    • Spending is likely to exceed $1 trillion next year.
    • Expenditures are projected to reach nearly $1.1 trillion by 2027.
    • Total AI capital investments from Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle (which partners with OpenAI) could exceed $5 trillion over the next four years.
  • Financial Impact:
    • Investments could soon reach around 3% of GDP.
    • Total AI revenues this year are expected to be between $150 billion and $200 billion.
    • Free cash flow for the group is expected to soon dip into negative territory.
    • Alphabet reported nearly $120 billion in revenues in the latest quarter, but AI infrastructure spending resulted in a free cash deficit of some $5.9 billion, its first shortfall since 2004.

💡 Why it matters

  • Productivity Requirements: To break even by 2030—accounting for depreciation, the cost of capital, and a 15% return—AI companies must increase their own productivity by a factor of 2.7.
  • Economic Risks:
    • If a productivity boom materializes, it could lead to economic growth similar to the US IT boom starting in the mid-1990s.
    • If it fails to materialize, the buildout could be the largest misallocation of capital in history, potentially leading to bankruptcy if companies fall behind on interest payments.
  • Technical Obsolescence:
    • Compute electronics, which represent about 60% of costs, feature GPU chip performance that roughly doubles every two years.
    • To remain competitive, owners of data centers coming online this year and next will need to spend billions more on next-generation chips by the end of the decade, or risk the centers becoming “hulks” and stranded assets.

#AI #DataCenters #Hyperscalers #CapitalInvestment

Source: What’s at stake in AI’s trillion-dollar gamble

item.title: Comprehensive Guide and Resource Hub for AI Agent Frameworks Updated
item.description:
Comprehensive Guide and Resource Hub for AI Agent Frameworks Updated

An interactive resource guide for AI agent frameworks, tools, and infrastructure has been updated. Built for developers who ship, the resource is a Next.js 14 web application designed for searching, filtering, and exploring AI agents.

🔍 Overview

This resource provides the most comprehensive, structured guide to AI agent frameworks, tools, and resources, featuring side-by-side comparisons and weekly updates.

⚙️ Key details

Tool/Framework Description
OpenAI Assistants API Orchestrates multi-agent systems with role-based collaboration
Alibaba multi-agent framework Distributed deployment and fault tolerance for production use
Claude SDK Official SDK with tool use, computer control, and streaming for Claude-native agents
AWS infrastructure Managed agents with Bedrock models, enterprise compliance, and auto-scaling deployment
Semantic Kernel Event-driven multi-agent framework merged for production workflows
Role-based simulation framework Multi-agent simulation for collaborative reasoning and task completion
Multi-agent framework runtime Includes a control plane for managing agent deployments at scale
  • Some frameworks evolve agent skills, prompts, and harness modules by merging diffs from parallel workers against held-out reward.

#AIAgents #DeveloperTools #AIInfrastructure #LLM

Source: ARUNAGIRINATHAN-K/awesome-ai-agents-2026
